answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a meaningful, slashable deposit before it can transact. A hollow identity with no stake is cheap to spawn by the thousands, but a bonded one risks real loss if it cheats, so spinning up a plume of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Like a glacier, reputation then accrues slowly over verified work, so an attacker must pay upfront capital plus months of honest history before a fake identity carries any weight.
